findings.reason: the deliverable's requirement "never inferred from the position of an element in a list of options" removes an inference that does not exist, and a worker following it would not know that carrying an absolute path, and naming the lookup failure, is what the measured failure needs.
findings.text: the Why claims the job's carried recipe had the option `--dev-bind` as its first element, but the product composes `fenced = [FENCE_BINARY, ...]` (`reckon/_worker_fence.py:1986`) and carries `"argv": list(fenced)` in the recipe, so a recipe built through `fence_argv` has `argv[0] == "bwrap"` and `argv[1] == "--dev-bind"` — measured on this tree; the real failure is that the program is a bare name resolved through PATH on the job node, which has no bwrap, so the prepare step's `execvp(prefix[0], ...)` raises before any naming message

findings.reason: the control as written can pass while the measured defect still reproduces, so the gate cannot prove the guard fires.
findings.text: the negative control requires running "the recipe whose first element is an option" as a program, a recipe the product cannot produce (first element is the fence program, verified above), so the red arm must hand-build an argv the code never emits and it shows neither the base failure that was measured nor that the new naming message replaces a real silent refusal

findings.reason: the two arms are redundant rather than wrong: the same property is proved by one recipe plus the absent-program case, so removing the split tightens the wording without changing what is delivered.
findings.text: "the recipe as the product builds it for a GPU job and for a CPU job" cannot distinguish two arms: `fence_argv` takes no partition or GPU input and the GPU/CPU difference lives in scheduler options, so both arms are byte-identical and neither can fail where the other passes

findings.reason: §11 is done and `1ba2f962ce` is an ancestor of HEAD, so every node dispatched for §12 starts from code containing that section and no declared wait would change order.
findings.text: `s12` appears in `plan-section-declarations` but in no `plan-section-depends-on` entry, although its Why rests on the prepare step §11 landed and it declares §11's two modules as its write paths

findings.reason: a cohort or cap sized from the plan's effort hours is short by the two sections' declared hours, and the scalar was exactly the section sum before those sections were added.
